roles.name: DevRel
roles.headline: Ship the release. Announce it everywhere, as you.
roles.lead: LinkedIn, X, Reddit, Hacker News, Bluesky, GitHub and Slack in one queue, posted from your own browser, signed in as you. Your agent drafts and dry-runs; you hold the switch.
roles.description: Blowhorn for developer relations: one queue for the networks developers use, including Hacker News and GitHub, posted as you from your own browser.

art.alt: Keyboard Warrior, a gold rooster in a teal helmet holding a keyboard with green keys like a shield

pains.b: Every release means seven composers and seven sign-ins, and the schedulers still skip Hacker News and GitHub.
Outreach tools ask for your password, your 2FA secret or your session cookie, then log in as you from their servers.
The post goes out, and the first hour is gone before the people who would amplify it notice.

gets.t: One desk for where developers talk
gets.b: Hacker News submit and comment, GitHub follow and react, Slack messages as you, plus LinkedIn, X, Reddit and Bluesky, from one queue.
Blowhorn does the typing and clicking in your own browser. No vendor server logs in as you, and nothing is branded "sent via Blowhorn".
Every action is scripted and takes --dry-run first. No model decides what to click, and only approved posts go out.

gets.t: A sound wave on release day
gets.b: Schedule the announcement and have every profile you add amplify it at the moment you pick.

agent.title: Release posts, drafted by your assistant
agent.body: Your assistant can draft the release posts straight from your changelog. faq.q: Will it make me look like a bot?
faq.a: Blowhorn types key by key at the pace you pick, caps itself (for example 2 Hacker News link submissions per profile per day) and always hands CAPTCHA and 2FA prompts to you. Nobody can promise a platform won't flag an account. Curious what sites can see about your browser?

faq.q: Does a computer have to be awake?
faq.a: One set up for the profile does. Install Blowhorn on as many computers as you like; any awake one keeps the schedule.

pains.b: Every client security review asks, and the honest answer is usually a vendor's server.
Antidetect browsers fake fingerprints to juggle profiles. That is not a story you want to tell a client.
When something goes out wrong, you need to show exactly what ran and stop it fast.

gets.b: Mutating commands take --dry-run, and --check-queue lists what a run would do. Show the client before anything publishes.
Pause one action while everything else keeps running, or pause every computer at once.
Each Blowhorn profile maps to its own browser profile on each computer. No fake fingerprints.
A person doesn't type into two browser windows at once, and neither does Blowhorn.
